transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-04

Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sana Patel (Aurora Head of Security), Diego Ramos (Aurora Platform), Evelyn Brooks (Aurora Product)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be rough):

Topics: SSO/SAML + IdP mapping; Audit logs and SIEM integration; Data retention and deletion; Encryption/KMS; SOC2 evidence access; Next steps for pilot gating.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: all right, hey everyone thanks for jumping on. we wanted to keep this one pretty focused on the governance items we promised last week. Sana, you had a few outstanding questions about audit logs and retention, i believe?
[00:12] Sana Patel: yeah thanks, Maya. main thing is, uh, we need clarity on where logs live during the POC, how long are they retained, can we ship them to our Splunk instance, and how do you handle PII in logs, like token prefixes or full prompts.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: yep totally reasonable. quick caveat — i'll probably mangle some product names, sorry — but the core is: for hosted POC mode we persist request and response metadata in our control plane for X days by default. full prompts are not retained unless customer enables prompt logging. we also have an audit-log stream that can be delivered to customer endpoints.
[00:45] Diego Ramos: when you say control plane, is that Redwood-managed? we can't have plaintext prompts leave our VPC for compliance unless we sign an addendum.
[00:53] Liam O'Connor: good callout. control plane is Redwood-managed for hosted. for dedicated or private deployments, obviously logs can be kept inside your VPC or on-prem; for hosted POC we can offer encrypted delivery to your syslog/Splunk collector so you can ingest logs without Redwood storing full-text long term. there's also a short-term cache for debugging.
[01:13] Sana Patel: so two threads — encrypted delivery to Splunk, and deletion. we need a retention matrix: what fields you store, retention length, and whether those fields are redacted. also need to know about key management — do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) during the pilot?
[01:28] Maya Chen: noted. quick answer: we support customer KMS for Private deployments; for hosted POCs we can do bring-your-own-key in some cases via a limited KMS integration. i'll confirm specifics and include that in the controls matrix.
[01:40] Evelyn Brooks: one more from product — on the logs schema, can we get a sample shape? even just the headers and which fields may include tokens or user ids. our privacy team wants to do a field-level mapping.
[01:52] Liam O'Connor: absolutely — i'll put a redacted sample. it'll show request_id, model, model_version, token_count, latency_ms, route, tenant_id, redacted_prompt_hash, and an optional prompt_snippet flag which is off by default. the field names i say may be slightly different in the shipping telemetry, i'll attach the exact schema.
[02:09] Diego Ramos: how frequent are the audit events? is every generation a line item, or are they batched? also, does Redwood provide an event to indicate model fallback or routing changes?
[02:21] Liam O'Connor: events are generated per request; we also emit system events: model fallback, capacity alerts, route decisions. you can choose per-stream granularity: full event stream or aggregated windows to reduce volume. each event has a timestamp and request_id.
[02:36] Sana Patel: what about retention for token-level logs — we have regulators that require PII deletion within 30 days and retention of metadata for 1 year. can you support that?
[02:47] Maya Chen: we can. Redwood's hosted defaults are 90 days for prompt artifacts and 365 days for metadata, but we can configure for pilot to 30 days for prompt artifacts. we'll need you to sign a data handling addendum for the shorter window and to enable redaction options.
[03:02] Diego Ramos: any automated purge API or do we rely on scheduled jobs?
[03:06] Liam O'Connor: there's a deletion API we expose for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we run scheduled retention purges but we can also trigger on-demand purge via an authenticated API for scoped requests during the pilot. i'll include the endpoint in the doc.
[03:20] Evelyn Brooks: and audit logs — can we keep an append-only log for compliance? like an immutable stream we can ship to our SIEM with an audit trail?
[03:29] Liam O'Connor: yes — we support signed append-only event streams. for hosted, we provide signed log batches with sequence numbers and a digest; when you ingest into Splunk or Datadog you can validate sequence. for Private, the events are locally stored and you control retention.
[03:44] Sana Patel: SOC2 — we need the Type II report and a controls matrix. is that available for pilot customers?
[03:51] Maya Chen: yes, i'll send a summary and the SOC2 Type II report redacted as needed. i will include the controls mapping to the telemetry and retention controls. note that the full report contains some vendor redactions but is accepted by most enterprise compliance teams.
[04:02] Sana Patel: do you have explicit controls around RBAC and least privilege for auditors? our auditors will want admin separation.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: RBAC is supported — you can create roles scoped to models, routes, and environmental access. for the pilot we can show a demo tenant with restricted admin roles, and we support SAML SSO with SCIM sync.
[04:23] Diego Ramos: SCIM — does it provision groups? our IAM relies heavily on groups mapping to roles.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: yes SCIM supports group push. we map SCIM groups to RBAC roles; that mapping is configurable in the admin console.
[04:37] [background murmur] Sana Patel: sorry quick Q about tokenization logging — do you log full tokens or hashes?
[04:43] Liam O'Connor: hashes by default, full tokens only if you opt-in for prompt logging for debugging. we also provide a prompt redaction pipeline that can remove email-like strings or SSNs. it's configurable with regex rules or using your PII detection hook.
[04:56] Maya Chen: can we pause for a sec — Diego had a question about legal access to logs in the rare case of subpoenas — who has authority?
[05:03] Diego Ramos: yeah, just to confirm what's the process and retention of legal holds.
[05:07] Liam O'Connor: legal holds — we support preservation windows and can snapshot logs for a legal hold. this requires an internal escalation and signed process; i'll put the escalation checklist in the doc. for hosted POCs we can preserve a snapshot for up to the pilot period plus a short extension.
[05:23] Sana Patel: great. small follow-up — encryption in transit and at rest? KMS?
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest. for private deployments you can bring your own key via customer KMS. for hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys for some customers. will confirm exactly which cloud KMS providers are supported in the follow-up.
[05:44] Evelyn Brooks: are there any limitations we should know about when running the workload that might affect logs? e.g., high-volume batching or KV cache that might redact or change request shapes?
[05:53] Liam O'Connor: good point — batching metadata is included as batch_id and request_indices. KV cache hits are indicated in the event payload but not the cached content; so you won't see the full cache contents in logs. that keeps logs smaller and avoids accidental leakage.
[06:07] Maya Chen: okay, next technical ask — Diego requested a small benchmark of log volume at our expected qps; Diego, do you have the numbers?
[06:14] Diego Ramos: for the pilot we're targeting 15 RPS average, maybe spikes up to 60 for short bursts. most requests are short chat-style prompts, avg 120 tokens.
[06:24] Liam O'Connor: rough rule of thumb: metadata-only events are ~1KB per request; with prompt snippets enabled more like 4-6KB. at 15 RPS metadata-only that's about 1.3GB/day; with snippets maybe 5GB/day. i'll include a sizing calc in the follow-up.
[06:43] Sana Patel: please include cost implications of shipping to Splunk vs storing in Redwood. Splunk ingestion costs are real.
[06:49] Maya Chen: understood — i'll call that out and include tradeoffs.
[06:53] [00:07:00-ish marker] Maya Chen: quick recap of decisions so far: Redwood will provide a retention matrix and schema, share SOC2 summary, set up an audit-log export demo to your Splunk instance, and support a 30-day prompt retention for PII during the pilot with appropriate addendum. action items will be in the notes.
[07:12] Diego Ramos: sounds good. one more operational question — if we want to switch to a Dedicated deployment mid-pilot, is there an easy migration path that preserves audit continuity?
[07:22] Liam O'Connor: yes, we support migration with a continuity plan: you can keep log streaming to the same SIEM and we keep sequence numbers consistent. there may be a short cutover window where logs are buffered; we'll document that.
[07:34] Evelyn Brooks: last question from product: are there prebuilt dashboards for security metrics? e.g., failed auth attempts, model fallback rates, peak latencies?
[07:42] Liam O'Connor: yes, Console includes per-route dashboards and security metrics. for SIEM we ship prebuilt ingestion pipelines and dashboard JSON for Splunk and Datadog. i'll share the dashboard JSONs.
[07:53] Sana Patel: thanks — this feels like a solid plan. can you confirm timing for the SOC2 doc and the Splunk demo?
[08:00] Maya Chen: i'll send SOC2 and controls by Friday (2026-08-06). Liam, can you take the Splunk demo next Tuesday?
[08:07] Liam O'Connor: yep, i'll prepare a 20-minute demo of the audit-stream export and an on-demand purge flow — propose 2026-08-11 at 15:00 UTC.
[08:15] Diego Ramos: works for me.
[08:17] Evelyn Brooks: same.
[08:18] Maya Chen: perfect. we'll also include a retention addendum draft for you to review.
[08:23] [small cross-talk] Sana Patel: okay, thanks everyone. looking forward to the demo and docs.
[08:27] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to the doc bundle: SOC2 summary, retention matrix, sample schema, and escalation checklist.
